newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan construction loans fall for 17th month.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan construction loans fall for 17th month.

text.p: The value of loans extended by Taiwan banks to construction firms fell 20.66 percent to T$394.43 billion in September from a year earlier, the central bank said on Monday.
September was the 17th consecutive month of declines. It followed an 18.54 percent year-on-year fall in August.
Loans extended by Taiwan banks to all private businesses fell 9.31 percent to T$2.874 trillion in September from a year earlier, the central bank also said.

September's overall decline was the sixth monthly fall in 10 years -- and all were in 1996. Lending fell 0.35 percent in January, 0.80 percent in May, 1.1 percent in June, 2.21 percent in July, and 4.95 percent in August.
Central bank officials had attributed the flat-to-negative recent growth to a persistent overall slowing in the economy.
Banks have been particularly cautious in granting loans to firms in the construction sector, which has seen deep recession since the local real estate market peaked in 1989.
In late August, the central bank scrapped all the selective credit controls on land, the latest in a series of moves to boost the real estate market and, in turn, the wider economy.
Analysts say the effects of the move should gradually become evident.
